generated_test_cases.title: Retrieve database session successfully
generated_test_cases.description: Test that get_db returns a valid database session when called during normal operation.
steps: Call get_db function to obtain a database session
Use the session to execute a simple query such as SELECT 1
expected_results: get_db returns a non-null session object
The query returns the expected result (e.g., 1)

generated_test_cases.title: Database session closed after use
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that the database session is properly closed after the context exits.
steps: Call get_db and store the session
Close the session explicitly using session.close()
Attempt to execute a query with the closed session
expected_results: Closing the session does not raise an exception
Executing a query with a closed session raises an exception indicating the session is closed

generated_test_cases.title: Handle database connection failure
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that get_db handles a connection failure gracefully and reports an error.
steps: Simulate a database connection failure (e.g., by providing an invalid connection URL)
expected_results: get_db raises an appropriate exception (e.g., sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError)

generated_test_cases.title: Prevent SQL injection via get_db
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that get_db does not expose vulnerabilities to SQL injection through session creation.
steps: Attempt to inject malicious input into any parameter used in get_db (none in this case)
expected_results: get_db executes without interpreting injected payload as SQL

generated_test_cases.title: Integration test with actual database
generated_test_cases.description: Test get_db integration with a real database by creating, querying, and cleaning up a test record.
steps: Call get_db to obtain a session
Insert a test record into the database
Query the record to verify insertion
expected_results: All database operations succeed without errors
The test record is correctly inserted, retrieved, and deleted

generated_test_cases.title: Dependency Error Handling on Successful Import
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that the dependency_error function correctly handles a successful dependency resolution and logs the success message.
preconditions: Import main.py without missing dependencies
Set up a mock dependency environment that returns success
steps: Call dependency_error with a mock dependency that resolves successfully
Verify that the function returns a success status
expected_results: The function should return True or a success indicator
A log entry indicating successful dependency resolution is created

generated_test_cases.title: Dependency Error Handling with Missing Dependency
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that the dependency_error function properly reports an error when a required dependency is missing.
preconditions: Import main.py without the required dependency
steps: Call dependency_error with a missing dependency
expected_results: The function should raise a DependencyError or return False

generated_test_cases.title: Boundary Case: Empty Dependency List
generated_test_cases.description: Test the function behavior when provided with an empty dependency list.
preconditions: Import main.py
Provide an empty list of dependencies
steps: Invoke dependency_error with an empty dependency list
expected_results: Function should handle gracefully, possibly returning True or no operation

generated_test_cases.title: Security: Dependency Injection Attack
generated_test_cases.description: Confirm that the dependency_error function does not execute arbitrary code from untrusted dependencies.
preconditions: Import main.py
Create a malicious dependency that attempts code injection
steps: Call dependency_error with the malicious dependency
expected_results: The function should sanitize input and reject the malicious dependency

generated_test_cases.title: Exception Handling: Unexpected Exception During Dependency Check
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that dependency_error correctly propagates or handles unexpected exceptions during dependency checking.
preconditions: Import main.py
steps: Simulate an unexpected exception (e.g., network failure) during dependency verification
expected_results: The function should catch the exception and return an appropriate error status or rethrow

generated_test_cases.title: Create Job - Successful
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that creating a new job with valid data returns 201 and the correct job representation.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/jobs/ with a JSON body containing a valid 'name' field.
expected_results: Response status code is 201.
Response body matches the JobOut schema with the same 'name' and a generated 'id'.

generated_test_cases.title: Create Job - Missing Name
generated_test_cases.description: Attempt to create a job without providing the required 'name' field to trigger validation error.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/jobs/ with an empty JSON object.
expected_results: Response status code is 422 (Unprocessable Entity).
Response body contains validation error indicating 'name' field is required.

generated_test_cases.title: Update Job - Dependency Not Up
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that updating a job fails when the required dependency state is not 'up', exercising the branch x_dependency_state != 'up'.
steps: Mock the dependency to return a state other than 'up'.
Send a PUT request to /api/jobs/123 with valid update data.
expected_results: Response status code is 409 (Conflict) or appropriate error defined by the dependency check.
Response body indicates that the dependency state is invalid.

generated_test_cases.title: Update Job - Successful
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that updating an existing job with valid data returns 200 and updated job details.
steps: Send a PUT request to /api/jobs/123 with a JSON body containing a new 'name' value.
expected_results: Response status code is 200.
Response body matches the JobOut schema with the updated 'name' and unchanged 'id' and 'state'.

generated_test_cases.title: Update Job - Non‑existent ID
generated_test_cases.description: Attempt to update a job that does not exist to trigger a 404 error.
steps: Send a PUT request to /api/jobs/999999 with valid update data.
expected_results: Response status code is 404 (Not Found).
Response body indicates that the job with the given ID does not exist.

generated_test_cases.title: Verify create job fails when dependency state is not up
generated_test_cases.description: Test that POST /api/jobs/ returns error when required dependency state is not 'up' and the system cannot proceed with job creation.
preconditions: Dependency 'require_dependency' is reported with state 'down' or 'maintenance'
steps: 2. Send POST request to /api/jobs/ with valid JobCreate payload.
expected_results: 1. Dependency state is 'down'.
2. API responds with 400 Bad Request or appropriate error status.
3. Response body contains error message indicating dependency is not up.

generated_test_cases.title: Verify create job succeeds when dependency state is up
generated_test_cases.description: Test that POST /api/jobs/ succeeds when required dependency state is 'up' and all conditions are met.
preconditions: Dependency 'require_dependency' is reported with state 'up'
steps: 2. Send POST request to /api/jobs/ with valid JobCreate payload.
expected_results: 1. Dependency state is 'up'.
2. API responds with 201 Created.
3. Response body contains created JobOut object with correct fields.

generated_test_cases.title: Load existing job successfully
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that load_job returns the job when a valid job ID is provided and the job exists.
steps: Create a job record in the test database.
Call load_job with the ID of the created job.
expected_results: The job object is returned and is not null.

generated_test_cases.title: Load job with missing ID
generated_test_cases.description: Confirm that load_job raises JobNotFoundError when the specified job does not exist.
steps: Ensure no job exists with ID 99999.
expected_results: JobNotFoundError is raised.

generated_test_cases.title: Validate transition to done when current state is done
generated_test_cases.description: Check that validate_transition accepts a transition to 'done' when the job is already in 'done' state.
steps: Create a job with state set to 'done'.
expected_results: No exception is raised and the transition is considered valid.

generated_test_cases.title: Reject invalid state transition
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure validate_transition raises JobConflictError when attempting to transition to an unsupported state.
expected_results: JobConflictError is raised because 'paused' is not in {'running','done'}.

generated_test_cases.title: Boundary test for state list
generated_test_cases.description: Test validate_transition with a state value that is exactly on the boundary of allowed values.
expected_results: Transition is accepted without error.

generated_test_cases.title: Security test for injection in job ID
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that load_job sanitizes input and does not allow SQL injection via job ID parameter.
steps: Call load_job with a malicious ID string "1; DROP TABLE jobs;--".
expected_results: JobNotFoundError or a safe error is raised; no database corruption occurs.

generated_test_cases.title: Create job with missing required fields
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure create_job raises DependencyUnavailableError when required dependencies are not available.
expected_results: DependencyUnavailableError is raised.

generated_test_cases.title: Nested Not Found Error Propagation
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure API returns proper 404 when a nested resource is not found during hierarchical lookup.
preconditions: Database contains parent resource but missing child resource
steps: 1. Start application with test data having parent but missing child.
2. Send API request targeting the nested child resource.
expected_results: 1. Application performs lookup for parent and child.
2. Child not found triggers a 404 Not Found response with clear message.
